# BTicino C300X Integration v1.9.8

## 2026-11-01

## Upgrade

- Requires Home Assistant `2026.7.0` or newer; automated validation targets
  `2026.7.0` and `2026.10.0`. HA 2026.5 and 2026.6 are no longer supported.
- Includes the freshly built native agent `1.9.8`, not the previous release's
  binary. Update the agent and core QML hook together, then reload the C300X GUI.
  Updating only the Home Assistant integration does not activate these fixes.

## Fixed

- Synchronize ringer mute/unmute with the GUI's saved audio state through the
  same AudioState operations as the device button (#65). Require GUI
  confirmation and device readback; fail explicitly when the GUI is unavailable.
- Correct the core call-end notification from port 8092 to the default UI port
  8090. Reapplying the core patch upgrades old hooks while preserving backups.

## Added

- Optional verified HTTPS for event and display callbacks through an explicit
  HTTPS callback base URL override. Requires an updated agent. HTTP does not
  initialize TLS. Changing HTTP/HTTPS modes restarts only the agent, deferred
  while media is active. HTTPS adds TLS work on the device, verifies certificate
  chains and hostnames, and never falls back to HTTP. Thanks to @Minims for the
  original verified HTTPS transport contribution in #61, adapted in #71.

## Changed

- Validate Home Assistant 2026.10 compatibility, using Probatio on HA 2026.9+
  and Voluptuous on older supported versions, including the camera API changes.
- Bundle routine dependency updates quarterly while keeping security updates
  independent. Align dependency manifests, CI and the supported HA minimum.
- Remove the on-demand teardown settle window introduced in 1.9.7. Hardware
  testing showed it did not prevent the PCMU reboot while delaying reconnects
  by up to 8 seconds. SIP-setup failure reasons remain available.
- Tear an on-demand session down by removing only the agent's own BT-AV UDP
  clients instead of issuing a global pipeline stop. Log unacknowledged
  removals, distinguishing a NACK from a missing ACK; a NACK can occur after
  SIP BYE has already removed the pipeline.
- Offer only PCMU in the on-demand SDP when the device codec is PCMU, instead of
  a full multi-codec offer, so the negotiated codec matches the configured one
  (#55).
- Preserve separate SIP messages received together over TCP, including an INVITE
  final response following `100 Trying`. Reassemble fragmented messages within
  a bounded deadline and reject incomplete or invalid frames.

## Known Limitations

- **PCMU on-demand device reboots (#55) remain unresolved.** This release is not
  a confirmed reboot fix; use `speex` to avoid the known PCMU-specific failure.
- Physical-device validation of the new ringer command path, exact HTTPS opt-in
  implementation and media reference flow is still pending. Automated tests and
  firmware analysis do not replace these checks. Issues #55 and #65 remain open.

## Release Assets

- One HACS installation archive with native agent and QML components, plus
  `SHA256SUMS`, `build-metadata.json` and an SPDX 2.3 SBOM.
- The release workflow generates and verifies SLSA provenance and SBOM
  attestations against this tag and its source commit before publication.
